title: A reductive DVR group embeds linearly with affine homogeneous quotient
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. An $A$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finite-type $A$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose its geometric fibres are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means consisting of unipotent matrices in a faithful representation over the geometric residue field. There exist $n\geq1$ and a homomorphism $i:H\hookrightarrow L=\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}$ which is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here $\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[x_{ab},d]/(d\det(x_{ab})-1)$, with multiplication of invertible matrices. The fppf sheaf quotient $Q=L/H$ is represented by an affine $A$-scheme, and its quotient map $q:L\to Q$ is a represented right $H$-torsor [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. The sheaf quotient is the sheafification of the presheaf of right cosets on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Both its representation and its torsor map commute with every base change of $A$-schemes. No splitness, completeness, or perfection of the residue field is assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf, Corollary 9.7.7, printed p.528 (affineness). Embedding: Milne, Basic Theory of Affine Group Schemes, VIII, Aside 9.4, printed pp.125--126, Dedekind-domain paragraph, read https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf. These are the two structural inputs in Alper--Halpern-Leistner--Heinloth Section 2, Claim 2.

proof.text: Put $B=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation by sbc-lem-smooth-criterion; affineness makes $H\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence finitely presented. The affine flatness criterion makes $B$ a flat $A$-module. Multiplication, identity and inverse give $B$ its coordinate Hopf $A$-algebra structure $\Delta$, $\epsilon$, $S_B$ [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. The affine fibre-product lemma identifies $H\times_AH$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AB)$, and likewise the triple product with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AB\otimes_AB)$, with projections induced by the tensor inclusions; by the affine spectrum dictionary and the tensor pushout universal property, morphisms between these spectra are exactly algebra maps between the tensor products, so the group diagrams are precisely the Hopf identities. Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$. Apply the finite-free lattice node to the regular coaction $\Delta:B\to B\otimes_AB$ and $T=\{1,b_1,\ldots,b_r\}$. Flatness over the domain $A$ implies torsion-freeness: tensor the injection $A\xrightarrow{a}A$ for $a\ne0$. We obtain a finite free stable submodule $V\subseteq B$ containing $T$. Since $\epsilon(1)=1$, its rank $n$ is at least one.

source.place: VIII, Aside 9.4, pp.125--126; Aside 4.7, p.117; affine Hopf construction in II and III.

proof.text: Choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $V$ and write $\Delta(e_j)=\sum_i e_i\otimes c_{ij}$. Coassociativity and the counit, by applying the coordinate maps of this finite free basis, give $\Delta(c_{ij})=\sum_kc_{ik}\otimes c_{kj}$ and $\epsilon(c_{ij})=\delta_{ij}$. Applying the antipode identities to these equations gives $\sum_kc_{ik}S_B(c_{kj})=\delta_{ij}=\sum_kS_B(c_{ik})c_{kj}$. Thus the matrix $C=(c_{ij})$ is invertible over $B$, and $x_{ij}\mapsto c_{ij}$, $d\mapsto\det(C)^{-1}$ defines an algebra map $A[x_{ij},d]/(d\det(x)-1)\to B$. Since $\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}\times_A\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}=\operatorname{Spec}$ of the tensor square of its coordinate ring by the affine fibre-product lemma, on which matrix multiplication is $x_{ij}\mapsto\sum_kx_{ik}\otimes x_{kj}$, the displayed comultiplication and counit identities say its spectrum map $i:H\to\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}$ respects multiplication and identity; inverse compatibility follows from uniqueness of an inverse. Moreover $e_j=(\epsilon\otimes1)\Delta(e_j)=\sum_i\epsilon(e_i)c_{ij}$. Its image therefore contains $V$, hence every generator $b_j$; the map is surjective. The affine quotient criterion in def-weil-closed-immersion makes $i$ a closed immersion. This constructs a scheme-theoretic embedding, not just an injection on geometric points.

source.place: VIII, Theorem 9.1 proof, p.125, coefficient calculation; Aside 9.4, pp.125--126.

proof.text: For $L=\operatorname{GL}_{n,A}$ use the left $H$-action $h\cdot l=l\,i(h)^{-1}$. Its orbits are the right cosets, and it is free on every test scheme: cancellation gives $i(h)=1$, and $i$ is injective on all test points: writing $P=A[x_{ij},d]/(d\det(x)-1)$, the affine fibre-product lemma gives $H\times_LH=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_PB)$, and $B\otimes_PB=B$ because $P\to B$ is surjective, so the diagonal of $i$ is an isomorphism and $i$ is a monomorphism. Apply the free-flat-group-space-quotient node with $B=S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=L$. The flatness and local finite presentation were checked in step 1. It supplies an algebraic space $Q$, a flat surjective locally finitely presented map $q:L\to Q$, fppf local sections, and the sheaf isomorphism $L\times_AH\simeq L\times_QL$, $(l,h)\mapsto(l,l\,i(h))$, after changing the order of the factors and replacing $h$ by $h^{-1}$.

The fibre assumptions of the item are exactly those of the reductive-ring-invariant-power-lifting node, which applies to $H$ using the finite presentation from step 1. It gives universal invariant power lifting for arbitrary equivariant algebra quotients over every $A$-algebra. Apply the power-reductive-free-affine-quotient node with $R=A$, $G=H$, $X=L$ and $Y=Q$. Here $L$ is affine by its displayed spectrum, the action is free by step 3, and the required algebraic space, local sections and torsor identity are all furnished there. Consequently $Q$ is an affine $A$-scheme and $q$ is affine finitely presented. Together with its flatness, surjectivity and right action, the identity in step 3 is exactly the represented right torsor definition.

Let $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be arbitrary. On $T$-schemes there is a natural map from the right-orbit presheaf of $L_T$ to $Q_T$. Every section of $Q_T$ lifts fppf locally to $L_T$: apply the local sections of $q$ to the composite test scheme $U\to Q_T\to Q$. If two local lifts have the same image, the sheaf isomorphism of step 3 gives a unique local $h\in H_T$ carrying one to the other. Thus this map becomes surjective and injective after sheafification and identifies the quotient sheaf with $Q_T$. The torsor identity itself pulls back to $L_T\times_TH_T\simeq L_T\times_{Q_T}L_T$ because its two maps and inverse are defined by the same functorial group operations on every test scheme. This identifies the base-changed quotient map as well as the representing object; the identifications are canonical by the sheaf universal property. No assertion about arbitrary base change of invariant coordinate rings is used.

Alper's paper is not in literature/, so I fetched it from the URL the node gives and read Def 3.1.1, Thm 4.3.1, Thm 9.1.4, Lemma 9.2.5, Prop 9.3.1(i), Thm 9.7.5 with its proof, Cor 9.7.7 and Prop 9.7.8. All three new nodes are true. (1) dvr-comodule-finite-free-lattice: with C flat over a Noetherian ring, Serre's argument works: take M'=ρ^{-1}(N⊗C), where N is spanned by the left factors of ρ(m); this M' is a finitely generated subcomodule containing m, and a torsion-free finitely generated module over a DVR is free. The empty set, M=0 and M=K all behave. (2) reductive-ring-invariant-power-lifting follows from Thm 9.7.5, then Prop 9.3.1(i), then Lemma 9.2.5 (2)⇒(3), with no Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis. (3) power-reductive-free-affine-quotient: the hypothesis is Lemma 9.2.5(3), which makes G geometrically reductive; Prop 9.7.8 (with Thm 4.3.1) then makes Y affine, and q is affine and f.p. by fppf descent from the trivial torsor. A DAG-wide search found no duplicate: the existing nodes are over a field, for PGL, or for split tori over a Noetherian base. No new node restates a clause of the item. Steps 2, 4 and 5 check out: the coefficient matrix is invertible via the antipode and its image contains the generators; the left action h·l = l i(h)^{-1} and the torsor isomorphism are right; the represented-right-torsor clause of def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors applies over an arbitrary base; fppf base change works. FIX for missing citations (C4/C5/C1). Step 1 attributed H×_AH=Spec(B⊗B) to def-weil-affine-spectrum plus the tensor-pushout lemma, which give only Spec-to-Spec maps; it also introduced the coordinate Hopf structure without citing the existing same-unit def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra. Step 2 used the same affine fibre-product fact for GL_n×GL_n. Step 3 claimed i is a monomorphism with no node behind it. The fix cites lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra (a Mathlib leaf, pullbackSpecIso) in steps 1–3 and def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra in step 1. Step 3 now proves the monomorphism property: H×_LH=Spec(B⊗_PB)=Spec B because P→B is surjective. proof_deps is recomputed; the statement and new nodes are unchanged, and there is no cycle. I accept the declared tool_uses (smooth criterion, flat-affine criterion, tensor pushout) as generic.
